newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia accepts Singapore leader's apology-Minister.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia accepts Singapore leader's apology-Minister.

text.p: Malaysia accepted Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's apology over a remark about a Malaysian state, but it will take time to restore damaged relations, Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said on Wednesday.
"The Malaysian government accepts the unreserved apology by Lee and views positively his intentions to retract the offending paragraph," he told a news conference.
"However, it should be acknowledged that this episode has deeply hurt Malaysians of all sections of society and that restoration of the old level of relationship would take time."
Lee said in a statement on Monday he would ask a local court to delete a remark in an affidavit that the Malaysian state of Johor "was notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".

That move followed a rare public apology last week by the 73-year-old Lee, who led the fight for Singapore's independence and was its prime minister from 1959 until 1990. He now has an elder statesman's role as senior minister.

Lee's remarks infuriated Kuala Lumpur -- which is sensitive to any perceived slurs from its traditionally more economically developed neighbour -- and last week the Foreign Ministry demanded an apology and a retraction.
